chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Arrangements on tour, and why she couldn't record 'Trees'
summary: She took about five arrangements on tour; a publisher issue kept her from singing 'Trees'.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Okay, so you were singing basically the same kind of material when you did that tour. How many arrangements would you have taken with you on that?

You never had to take any more than five arrangements because on the vaudeville stage you're limited. You're working with five or six other acts. And I remember when I first went into Loews State, I went in there with ten or twelve songs. I thought I was going to be out there all day. I sang about five songs and the management came back and said look, keep it down to twelve minutes or else. So you really didn't need much music, you know, but you did the same thing every where you went.
Okay can I ask you something else? Considering the success of the song 'Trees' for you before you came to New York, how come that never appeared on record?
I have no idea. There's a possibility that I might have gotten sort of scared off of it because, you know, when I opened at Loews State, the first appearance on stage, I did 'Trees' and the
